scope: Standing Aga Khan Palace exterior in Pune, from its mapped forecourt steps and fountain through the arcaded palace ranges to the rear wings. Museum interiors, detached buildings and memorials are outside this model’s scope.

sources.use: Maha Metro’s updated detailed project report lists Italian arches, five halls, a 2.5 m surrounding corridor and three floor areas of 1,756, 1,080 and 445 square metres.
INTACH Pune describes the Gothic Indian balustrades on all elevations, Indo-Saracenic finials and a pointed opening with jali above the entrance porch.
The Pune site survey describes stuccoed brick, a stone plinth, hipped tiled pavilion roofs, Gothic clerestory tracery and rose windows, and dark stone columns below a pale upper balustrade.
The site survey identifies three round entrance arches, the patron’s medallions, and the roof gables of the entrance hall.
The Ministry of Culture confirms current ASI conservation and national monument identity.

omitted.reason: Original anonymous photograph is dated only before 1948. The native record supplies a public-domain basis for India and leaves first publication and US status unresolved.
The exact Qualla bytes match the photographer’s native worldwide public-domain release. Its subject is the separately located memorial, outside the named palace structure.

imageryScreen.selected: The existing Qualla images were screened first. The confirmed public-domain photograph shows the nearby ashes memorial. The historical palace photograph has unresolved first publication and US status. The reconstruction uses the mapped standing footprint, original terrain and written architectural surveys.
